s1.syndrome_frame: A congenital, slowly growing, exophytic oral lesion
salient_findings: 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion present since birth with no change in size or character
MRI showing a partly fatty, submucosal mass with mild contrast enhancement and intact overlying mucosa
key_facts: 20-year-old man with no significant medical history
Lesion located on the midline of the dorsal tongue
Lesion is 1.5-cm in diameter
Lesion is exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft
Lesion has been present since birth
Lesion has not changed in size or character over time
Vital signs are within normal limits
MRI shows a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue
Lesion appears partly fatty and submucosal on MRI
Lesion demonstrates mild contrast enhancement on MRI
Overlying mucosa is intact
No involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
Sublingual space and major salivary glands appear normal

shortlist.label: Congenital granular cell epulis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a congenital, exophytic oral lesion

shortlist.label: Lingual thyroid
shortlist.why_kept: Could present as a midline tongue mass, although less common

shortlist.label: Congenital lingual dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a congenital, slowly growing oral lesion

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Partly fatty appearance on MRI is consistent with lipoma

shortlist.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Could present as a midline neck or tongue mass, although typically not exophytic

raw.rationale: The lesion's presence since birth, location on the midline of the dorsal tongue, and partly fatty appearance on MRI are consistent with a congenital lingual dermoid cyst.

rejected.label: Congenital granular cell epulis
rejected.why: Typically presents in infancy and is more common in females

rejected.label: Lingual thyroid
rejected.why: Would likely show increased uptake on thyroid scans and have a different appearance on MRI

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Although partly fatty, the lesion's location and presence since birth are more suggestive of a congenital dermoid cyst

rejected.label: Thyroglossal duct cyst
rejected.why: Typically presents in the midline of the neck, not on the tongue
